newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JULY 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JULY 23.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The US on Tuesday expressed its respect for Prime Minister Costas Simitis and Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos on Tuesday, via US State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns, who is soon expected to be posted to Athens as US ambassador. Burns said Simitis was a "particularly strong" leader and had a clear vision of how to maintain stability in the eastern Mediterranean. Burns also said the prospects for a resolution of the Cyprus issue were the best since the 60s.

--Conservative opposition New Democracy deputies staged their first mutiny since the election of president Costas Karamanlis on Tuesday, voting against a bill on education in Parliament and breaching party unity.
--Fines will be imposed on passengers and shipowners for those passengers buying tickets on ferries rather than in advance.
--The agriculture ministry is facing criticism over its draft measures to protect animals. One of the measures under fire is the putting down of stray dogs if they show any aggression.
--New therapies being implemented at an Athens clinic have seen the fatality rate for AIDS cases reduced by 25 percent, according to reports.
--A number of Greek names are included on the list of pre-1945 account holders who may have perished in the Holocaust released to the press by Swiss banks on Tuesday.
--Development Minister Vasso Papandreou has filed suit for defamation against Eleftheros Typos and calls for damages of two billion drachmas, according to reports.
--A policeman was arrested on Tuesday for narcotics abuse. The father of five was arrested along with his wife and friend while they were shooting heroin.

--Police set up roadblocks on Tuesday to apprehend the leading suspect in the murder of a Greek Orthodox priest in suburban Athens. Forty-two-year-old housewife Katerina Yiannakopoulou is still at large.
